paragraph: Section 67 returns to aspheric objects and aspheric functors as the organizing notions for modelizers, taking up the earlier discussion of test categories and the preceding work on contractibility and homotopy structures. On pages 188–189 Grothendieck introduces the localizations (Hot_A^W), also written (Hot_A), and asks how they vary with A. Page 190 records the comparison morphism lambda_i from i_A i^* to i_B, gives its component on the categories of pairs (a,p), and interprets it through the induced morphism of topoi. The section ends on page 191 by preparing formulations in terms of i^* for the coming asphericity structures and testing functors. Section 72 explicitly resumes this discussion at page 213 and reuses the comparison triangle. The dated marginal note of 3.5 on page 189 revises the attribution to Quillen: Grothendieck calls his preceding assertion a misrepresentation and says that Quillen's weak equivalences are stronger than W_A; this authorial correction belongs in the guide without a further mathematical emendation. The witnesses differ materially on page 188, where the scan writes 'or' between the two Hot notations and retains a subscript A on W, and on page 190, where the handwritten source and target A/F to B/F of the map of pairs are absent from the arXiv formula.
status: section checked; later section 72 cross-reference verified in supplied witness

paragraph: Section 68 records the six-week interruption of the asphericity discussion and places the work on stacks among Grothendieck's concurrent interests. Pages 191–192 connect the Lego-Teichmüller construction game, surface cutting and gluing, moduli multiplicities, and the action of profinite Galois groups with his earlier La Longue Marche work. Pages 193–194 explain the alternation between mathematical work and personal reflection, and his intention to return to the Teichmüller questions after the present notes. The mathematical explanation on page 195 uses carefully chosen families of basepoints and presentations of groupoids; Grothendieck reports his own earlier attempts to work with groups or exterior groups and describes the change in his preferred formulation. He identifies the relevant modular multiplicities with topoi and explains how their automorphism groups enter the proposed generators for Teichmüller groupoids. This digression follows section 67 and prepares the retrospective of technical scratchwork begun in section 69; it does not supply a new proof needed by the asphericity criteria later resumed in section 72. The page check preserves the typed and handwritten layers of this account, including the handwriting at the clipped end of groups on page 192; that reading remains doubtful.

Section 69 turns the retrospective toward the extra structure carried by families of derived categories. Starting from the SGA 5 trace formalism and the work of Verdier, Deligne and Illusie, pages 196–197 consider I↦D_A(I), with D_A(I)=D(Hom(I,A)), and ask for formal properties of its dependence on the diagram category. Grothendieck introduces the adjoints f_! and f_* to f^*, calling their special cases integration and cointegration; page 198 relates them to amalgamated sums, fiber products and the Dold–Puppe sequences. The basic modelizer (Cat) from the preceding discussion supplies the cofibered-category construction of integration on page 199. Page 200 names the resulting structure a derivator and uses I×J to explain the desired stability under passing to diagram categories. Pages 201–202 connect this construction with the stratified moduli spaces and Teichmüller groupoids discussed in section 68, and record the change from expecting finite limits in (Hot) to requiring a diagram at the model level. Section 70 immediately uses the proposed factorization condition for the adjoints, while section 71 returns to derivators and their extension beyond categories of diagrams. The scan matters in several places: page 198 types T in the sentence about inverse limits where arXiv prints D; page 199 has q=f∘p and basic modelizer where the witness has g and basic localizer; page 200 uses a mapsto symbol in the defining assignment, where arXiv uses a plain arrow. These readings are retained, and the guide records the differences without silently identifying the printed symbols.
